segments.narration: A sealed 800-pound metal tube was lowered into a New York park. This wasn't military ordnance, but a meticulously engineered artifact designed to outlast modern civilization.
Forged from a revolutionary copper alloy named Cupaloy, metallurgists promised it would resist corrosion for five millennia.
Inside rested everyday items of the era: a fountain pen, a pack of cigarettes, and a alphabet block set.
Engineers buried the torpedo-shaped vault fifty feet underground at the Flushing Meadows site for the 1939 World's Fair.
It remains entombed in concrete, waiting silently for the calendar to finally reach the year 6939.
